anomalies.observed: The UART3 receive and transmit nets are attached to FCC1 pins 73 and 48, which the MCU symbol names VCAP. Those are the core-regulator decoupling output pins (power_out), not UART signal pins. The UART3 connector UART3_FCC1 therefore shares nets with the VCAP pins.
anomalies.expected: UART3 RX/TX should land on dedicated USART3 alternate-function pins (signal I/O), and VCAP pins should only have their own decoupling capacitors to ground.
anomalies.impact: The UART3 link to the connector cannot work, and the VCAP output (about 1.2 V core supply) is loaded by and shorted to a signal line, which can disturb MCU core regulation and the UART interface.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW pin 1 (A0) is tied to the +3.3V rail, while A1 to A5 are tied to GND. This sets the address bit A0 high.
anomalies.expected: The specification gives the PCA9685 I2C address as 0x40, which requires A0 to be tied to GND (all address pins low). With A0 high the device responds at 0x41.

evidence.quote: | PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40 |

anomalies.impact: The flight control computer will not communicate with the servo driver at the expected address, so servo/PWM outputs will not be driven.

anomalies.observed: GPIO_H_FCC has only the R47 pin 2 node. The matching FCC1 pin 55 (PD8) sits on its own unconnected net, while the other GPIO lines GPIO_A to GPIO_G each reach an FCC1 PD pin.
anomalies.expected: The eighth GPIO line should connect R47 pin 2 to an FCC1 port pin, as the other seven do.
anomalies.impact: The H-channel GPIO link between the two computers is open, so that signal cannot be exchanged.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the UART3 signals wired to the H753 VCAP power-output pins, a clear misconnection, and the PCA9685 A0 pin tied high, which moves the servo driver address from the specified 0x40 to 0x41. I rank the UART3/VCAP fault highest, with the PCA9685 address second.
